library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Krippendorff_2012_zalutumumab_cyno"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Krippendorff_2012_zalutumumab_cyno"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1007/s10928-012-9243-7> (open access, PMC3333800)

Krippendorff, Oyarzun and Huisinga replaced the Michaelis-Menten target term
of the cynomolgus-monkey zalutumumab PK model of Lammerts van Bueren et al.
(2006) with a cell-level model of EGF receptor (EGFR) trafficking. Each
target-expressing cell carries free surface receptor `R`, internalised free
receptor `Ri`, EGF-bound (activated) receptor `RL` and antibody-bound receptor
`RC`. The cell-level binding fluxes are scaled to the whole body by the number
of relevant cells `Ncell`, which is computed (not fitted) so that the cells'
total binding capacity equals the PK model's `Bmax,PK` (Eq. 17). No parameter
was estimated: the PK backbone is inherited (Table 1), the receptor rate
constants are in vitro fibroblast values (Table 2) and the antibody
affinities come from the literature (Table 4).

The packaged model is the extended system of Eqs. 30-40: normal cells plus a
tumour-cell population numbering 1% of the normal cells. Setting
`frac_tumor = 0` removes the tumour cells' effect on the PK and recovers the
single-cell-type model of Eqs. 19-24 (used for Figs. 3 and 4); the tumour
states then still respond to the interstitial concentration but no longer
feed back on it.

# Population

The PK data are from cynomolgus monkeys given single intravenous doses of 2,
20 and 40 mg/kg zalutumumab (Lammerts van Bueren et al. 2006; Fig. 3a data
courtesy of Genmab; the number of animals is not reported in this paper).
All amounts and volumes in the model are per kg body weight, so no body
weight covariate is needed. The receptor-system rate constants were measured
in human fibroblasts; for monkeys the paper multiplies the recycling rate
constant `krecyRi` by 4 and the free-receptor internalisation rate constant
`kdegR` by 1/4 (Table 2 footnote). The tumour cells are a hypothetical in
silico population exposed to the same interstitial concentration as normal
cells.

# Source trace

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| `d/dt(central)` | Eq. 30 | Plasma: `Vpla dCpla/dt = -qpi Cpla + qip Cint - CLlin Cpla` |
| `d/dt(isf)` | Eqs. 31-32 | Interstitial: transfer plus `N (koffC SFunit RC - konC SFunit R Cint)` for normal and tumour cells |
| `d/dt(target_*)`, `d/dt(target_int_*)`, `d/dt(complex_egf_*)`, `d/dt(complex_*)` | Eqs. 33-40 | Receptor trafficking per normal (N) and tumour (T) cell |
| Initial conditions | Methods | Pre-treatment steady state of `R`, `Ri`, `RL`; `RC(0) = 0`; bolus into plasma |
| `n_normal` | Eq. 17 | `Ncell = kdegRC Bmax,PK / (ksynR SFunit)` |
| `sf_unit` | after Eq. 11 | `SFunit = 1e9 / Navo` |
| `rl_pct_*`, `sat_*` | Eqs. 25-26 | Residual receptor activity `RL/RL*` and saturation `RC/(R+RL+RC)` |
| `lvc` | 70 mL/kg | Table 1, `V pla` |
| `lvisf` | 35 mL/kg | Table 1, `V int` |
| `lk12`, `lk21` | 0.043 1/h each | Table 1, `k pi`, `k ip`; `qpi = Vpla kpi`, `qip = Vint kip` |
| `lkel` | 0.0055 1/h | Table 1, `kel`; `CLlin = Vpla kel` |
| `bmax_pk` | 2 mg/kg | Table 1, `B max,PK` |
| `kon_egf` | 7.2e-2 1/(nM min) | Table 2, `konL` |
| `koff_egf` | 0.34 1/min | Table 2, `koffL` |
| `kint_target` | 0.03 1/min | Table 2, `kdegR` |
| `kint_egf` | 0.03 1/min | Table 2, `kdegRL` |
| `ksyn_target` | 130 receptors/min per cell | Table 2, `kR,N` |
| `krecy_target` | 5.8e-2 1/min | Table 2, `krecyRi` |
| `kdeg_target_int` | 2.2e-3 1/min | Table 2, `kdegRi` |
| `kint` | 0.005 1/h | Table 2, `kdegRC` |
| `mw` | 148000 g/mol | Table 2, `MWmAbs` |
| `f_recy_cyno`, `f_kint_cyno` | 4, 1/4 | Table 2 footnote |
| `egf` | 2.36e-3 nM | Text after Eq. 6 |
| `navo` | 6.02e23 1/mol | Text after Eq. 11 |
| `kon` | `= konL` | Table 2, `konC = konL` |
| `kd_invitro` | 7 nM | Table 4, zalutumumab 7e-9 M |
| `sfiviv` | 2.1 | Results, "Evaluation against in vivo data"; equals `KM,cell / KM,PK`, so in vivo `KD = KD(in vitro) / 2.1` (Eq. 18 orientation; see Assumptions and deviations) |
| `frac_tumor` | 0.01 | Text before the Methods: tumour cells 1% of normal cells |
| `fold_ksyn_tumor` | 10 | Fig. 5 caption: 10-fold increased receptor expression |
| `f_kint_drug` | 1 (5 and 10 in Fig. 4b-d) | Results, "Downregulation"; `Ncell` keeps the zalutumumab value |
| `fold_kint_tumor` | 1 (0.1 for the decreased-internalisation tumour) | Fig. 5 caption |

# Helpers

```{r helpers}
mod <- readModelDb("Krippendorff_2012_zalutumumab_cyno")
mod_obj <- rxode2::rxode2(mod)

# Typical parameter vector, from which scenario overrides are built.
theta <- mod_obj$theta

obs_h <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 24, by = 1), seq(24, 24 * 120, by = 6))))

solve_dose <- function(dose_mgkg, ..., times = obs_h) {
  pars <- theta
  over <- c(...)
  pars[names(over)] <- over
  ev <- rxode2::et(amt = dose_mgkg, cmt = "central", time = 0) |>
    rxode2::et(times)
  rxode2::rxSolve(mod_obj, events = ev, params = pars, returnType = "data.frame",
                  atol = 1e-10, rtol = 1e-8, maxsteps = 1e6) |>
    dplyr::mutate(dose = dose_mgkg)
}
```

# Pre-treatment steady state

Without drug, every receptor state must hold at the analytic steady state used
for the initial conditions, and the tumour cells with 10-fold increased
synthesis carry exactly 10 times the receptor of normal cells.

```{r steady-state}
ss <- solve_dose(0, times = seq(0, 24 * 60, by = 24))
drift <- ss |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    target = max(abs(target_normal / target_normal[1] - 1)),
    target_int = max(abs(target_int_normal / target_int_normal[1] - 1)),
    complex_egf = max(abs(complex_egf_normal / complex_egf_normal[1] - 1)),
    tumor = max(abs(target_tumor / target_tumor[1] - 1))
  )
knitr::kable(signif(drift, 3), caption = "Maximum relative drift over 60 days with no dose.")
stopifnot(all(unlist(drift) < 1e-6))
stopifnot(abs(ss$target_tumor[1] / ss$target_normal[1] - 10) < 1e-8)
c(R_star = ss$target_normal[1], Ri_star = ss$target_int_normal[1],
  RL_star = ss$complex_egf_normal[1])
```

# Derived quantities reported in the paper

The paper reports two computed quantities: the number of relevant cells
`Ncell = 5.2e9` (Eq. 17) and the in vitro-in vivo scaling factor
`SFiviv = 2.1`. Both are reproduced from the Table 1 and Table 2 values.

```{r derived}
th <- as.list(theta)
sf_unit <- 1e9 / th$navo
ksyn_h <- th$ksyn_target * 60
bmax_nmol <- th$bmax_pk / th$mw * 1e6
n_cell <- th$kint * bmax_nmol / (ksyn_h * sf_unit)

# Eq. 15 with the monkey rate constants (per min), in vitro KD = 7 nM
kdegR <- th$kint_target * th$f_kint_cyno
krecy <- th$krecy_target * th$f_recy_cyno
kdegRC_min <- th$kint / 60
koffC_min <- th$kd_invitro * th$kon_egf
drug_part <- (kdegRC_min + koffC_min) / (kdegRC_min * th$kon_egf)
system_part <- th$kdeg_target_int * kdegR / (th$kdeg_target_int + krecy) +
  th$egf * th$kon_egf * th$kint_egf / (th$koff_egf + th$kint_egf)
km_cell <- drug_part * system_part # nM
km_pk <- 0.5e-3 / th$mw * 1e9 # Table 1: KM,PK = 0.5e-3 mg/mL, in nM

tibble::tibble(
  Quantity = c("Ncell (cells/kg)", "KM,cell (nM)", "KM,PK (nM)", "KM,cell / KM,PK"),
  Reproduced = signif(c(n_cell, km_cell, km_pk, km_cell / km_pk), 3),
  Paper = c("5.2e9", "", "", "SFiviv = 2.1")
) |>
  knitr::kable()
stopifnot(abs(n_cell / 5.2e9 - 1) < 0.01)
stopifnot(abs(km_cell / km_pk - 2.1) < 0.01)
```

`Ncell` matches when `Bmax,PK` is read as an amount (2 mg/kg, as Eqs. 2-3 and
17 require), not the "mg/h/kg" printed in Table 1. The reported `SFiviv = 2.1`
equals `KM,cell / KM,PK`, the reciprocal of Eq. 18 as printed
(`KM,PK = SFiviv KM,cell` would give 0.48); see Assumptions and deviations.

# Figure 3a: plasma concentrations

The dashed lines are the Lammerts van Bueren Michaelis-Menten model of
Eqs. 1-3 with the Table 1 values (coded inline here for comparison only); the
solid lines are the packaged cell-level model with normal cells only
(`frac_tumor = 0`, the Fig. 3 configuration).

```{r figure-3a}
mm_mod <- rxode2::rxode2({
  vpla <- 70
  vint <- 35
  q_pi <- vpla * 0.043
  q_ip <- vint * 0.043
  cl_lin <- vpla * 0.0055
  kb <- 0.069
  bmax <- 2
  km <- 0.5e-3
  c_int <- isf / vint
  d/dt(central) <- -q_pi * central / vpla + q_ip * c_int - cl_lin * central / vpla
  d/dt(isf) <- q_pi * central / vpla - q_ip * c_int - kb * (bmax * c_int / (km + c_int) - bound)
  d/dt(bound) <- kb * (bmax * c_int / (km + c_int) - bound) - 0.0055 * bound
  Cc <- 1000 * central / vpla
})
mm_bound0 <- 0 # Methods: no drug-receptor complex before dosing
sim_mm <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(c(2, 20, 40), function(d) {
  ev <- rxode2::et(amt = d, cmt = "central") |> rxode2::et(obs_h)
  rxode2::rxSolve(mm_mod, ev, inits = c(bound = mm_bound0), returnType = "data.frame") |>
    dplyr::mutate(dose = d, model = "Michaelis-Menten (Eqs. 1-3)")
}))

sim_n <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(c(2, 20, 40), function(d) solve_dose(d, frac_tumor = 0))) |>
  dplyr::mutate(model = "Cell-level (Eqs. 19-24)")

dplyr::bind_rows(sim_n, sim_mm) |>
  dplyr::filter(dplyr::between(time, 1, 24 * 35), Cc >= 0.05) |>
  ggplot(aes(time / 24, Cc, colour = factor(dose), linetype = model)) +
  geom_line() +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Time (days)", y = "Plasma zalutumumab (ug/mL)", colour = "Dose (mg/kg)",
       linetype = NULL, caption = "Replicates Figure 3a of Krippendorff 2012.") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.box = "vertical")
```

```{r figure-3a-check}
cmp_pk <- dplyr::inner_join(
  sim_n |> dplyr::select(dose, time, Cc_cell = Cc),
  sim_mm |> dplyr::select(dose, time, Cc_mm = Cc),
  by = c("dose", "time")
) |>
  dplyr::filter(dplyr::between(time, 1, 24 * 21)) |>
  dplyr::group_by(dose) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    `Median |cell/MM - 1| (%), days 0-21` = round(100 * median(abs(Cc_cell / Cc_mm - 1)), 1),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
knitr::kable(cmp_pk)
# The two structures differ only in the target term. At 20 and 40 mg/kg the
# target is saturated and both reduce to the same linear PK; at 2 mg/kg they
# agree because the scaled KD makes the cell model's KM equal KM,PK. Reading
# the reported 2.1 the other way round puts the 2 mg/kg curves over 300% apart.
stopifnot(all(cmp_pk[[2]][cmp_pk$dose >= 20] < 3), cmp_pk[[2]][cmp_pk$dose == 2] < 15)
```

# Figure 3b and Table 3: receptor activation and saturation

```{r figure-3b}
sim_n |>
  dplyr::filter(dose %in% c(2, 20)) |>
  dplyr::select(time, dose, `Residual EGFR activation (%)` = rl_pct_normal,
                `Receptor saturation (%)` = sat_normal) |>
  dplyr::mutate(`Receptor saturation (%)` = 100 * `Receptor saturation (%)`) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-c(time, dose)) |>
  dplyr::filter(time <= 24 * 60) |>
  ggplot(aes(time / 24, value, linetype = factor(dose))) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~name) +
  labs(x = "Time (days)", y = "%", linetype = "Dose (mg/kg)",
       caption = "Replicates Figure 3b (main panel and inset) of Krippendorff 2012.")
```

```{r table-3}
tab3 <- sim_n |>
  dplyr::group_by(dose) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    max_sat = 100 * max(sat_normal),
    min_rl = min(rl_pct_normal),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(paper = c("Max. 60% saturated", "100% saturated", "100% saturated"))
tab3 |>
  dplyr::mutate(max_sat = round(max_sat, 1), min_rl = round(min_rl, 1)) |>
  dplyr::rename("Dose (mg/kg)" = dose, "Max saturation (%)" = max_sat,
                "Min residual activation (%)" = min_rl, "Paper, Table 3" = paper) |>
  knitr::kable()
stopifnot(
  abs(tab3$max_sat[tab3$dose == 2] - 60) < 7,
  all(tab3$max_sat[tab3$dose >= 20] > 98)
)

# Text: 20 mg/kg "almost completely inhibited receptor activation for a period
# of about 20 days", recovery starting between days 20 and 25.
rl20 <- sim_n |> dplyr::filter(dose == 20)
stopifnot(
  max(rl20$rl_pct_normal[rl20$time >= 24 & rl20$time <= 24 * 20]) < 10,
  rl20$rl_pct_normal[rl20$time == 24 * 30] > 25
)
```

Table 3 and the 20 mg/kg time course are reproduced: peak saturation at
2 mg/kg is 65% (Table 3: "Max. 60%"), and 20 mg/kg holds activated receptors
near zero for about 20 days. The text says 2 mg/kg "reduces the number of
active receptors by about 35%"; the model's nadir is 35% *of* baseline (a 65%
reduction), mirroring the saturation, so the sentence most likely means
"reduces to about 35%". See Assumptions and deviations.

# Figure 4: affinity, downregulation and the effect plateau

Different affinities are realised through `koffC` with `konC` fixed
(Results, "Affinity and dose"); each in vitro `KD` is divided by `SFiviv = 2.1`.

```{r figure-4a}
mabs <- tibble::tribble(
  ~mab,          ~kd_nM,
  "Panitumumab", 0.05,
  "Cetuximab",   0.4,
  "IMC-11F8",    0.3,
  "Nimotuzumab", 1,
  "Zalutumumab", 7
)
sim_mabs <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(mabs)), function(i) {
  dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(c(2, 20), function(d) {
    solve_dose(d, frac_tumor = 0, kd_invitro = mabs$kd_nM[i]) |>
      dplyr::mutate(mab = mabs$mab[i])
  }))
}))
sim_mabs |>
  dplyr::filter(time <= 24 * 60) |>
  ggplot(aes(time / 24, rl_pct_normal, colour = mab, linetype = factor(dose))) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(x = "Time (days)", y = "Active receptors (% of pre-treatment)",
       colour = NULL, linetype = "Dose (mg/kg)",
       caption = "Replicates Figure 4a of Krippendorff 2012.")
```

The three measures of Eqs. 27-28 and the duration of inhibition (time from
dosing until the activated receptors recover to 75% of baseline) are computed
over a 120-day horizon.

```{r inhibition-measures}
measures <- function(sim, rl_col = "rl_pct_normal") {
  rl <- sim[[rl_col]] / 100
  t <- sim$time
  integral <- sum(diff(t) * ((1 - rl[-1]) + (1 - rl[-length(rl)])) / 2) # receptor-fraction x h
  i_min <- which.min(rl)
  rec <- which(rl[i_min:length(rl)] >= 0.75)[1]
  duration <- if (min(rl) >= 0.75) 0 else t[i_min + rec - 1]
  c(integral_d = integral / 24, peak = 1 - min(rl), duration_d = duration / 24)
}

grid <- tidyr::expand_grid(kd_nM = 10^seq(-2, 2, by = 0.5), f_int = c(1, 5, 10), dose = c(2, 20))
fig4 <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(grid)), function(i) {
  g <- grid[i, ]
  s <- solve_dose(g$dose, frac_tumor = 0, kd_invitro = g$kd_nM, f_kint_drug = g$f_int)
  dplyr::bind_cols(g, tibble::as_tibble(as.list(measures(s))))
}))
fig4 |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(integral_d, peak, duration_d)) |>
  ggplot(aes(kd_nM / theta[["sfiviv"]], value, colour = factor(f_int), linetype = factor(dose))) +
  annotate("rect", xmin = 0.05 / 2.1, xmax = 7 / 2.1, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, alpha = 0.15) +
  geom_line() +
  scale_x_log10() +
  facet_wrap(~name, scales = "free_y",
             labeller = as_labeller(c(integral_d = "Integral (days)", peak = "Peak (fraction)",
                                      duration_d = "Duration (days)"))) +
  labs(x = "In vivo KD (nM)", y = NULL, colour = "kdegRC multiplier", linetype = "Dose (mg/kg)",
       caption = "Replicates Figure 4b-d of Krippendorff 2012; shaded: the five antibodies.")
```

```{r figure-4-check}
plateau <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(mabs)), function(i) {
  s <- sim_mabs |> dplyr::filter(mab == mabs$mab[i], dose == 20)
  tibble::tibble(mab = mabs$mab[i], tibble::as_tibble(as.list(measures(s))))
}))
knitr::kable(plateau |> dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(-mab, ~ signif(.x, 3))),
             caption = "Inhibition measures at 20 mg/kg for the five antibodies.")
# Effect plateau: a 140-fold affinity range changes the 20 mg/kg integral of
# inhibition by only a few percent.
stopifnot(diff(range(plateau$integral_d)) / max(plateau$integral_d) < 0.1)

# Downregulation (Results): negligible for high-affinity antibodies, a gain
# for lower-affinity ones.
hi_aff <- fig4 |>
  dplyr::filter(kd_nM <= 1) |>
  dplyr::group_by(kd_nM, dose) |>
  dplyr::summarise(spread = diff(range(integral_d)) / max(integral_d), .groups = "drop")
lo_aff <- fig4 |> dplyr::filter(kd_nM == 100, dose == 20)
stopifnot(
  nrow(hi_aff) == 10,
  all(hi_aff$spread < 0.02),
  lo_aff$integral_d[lo_aff$f_int == 10] > 1.05 * lo_aff$integral_d[lo_aff$f_int == 1]
)
```

# Figure 5: normal versus tumour cells

Two tumour-cell types with comparable 10-fold elevated EGFR (`R*` is 10.0-
and 9.9-fold the normal value): increased
receptor synthesis (`fold_ksyn_tumor = 10`, the model default) or 10-fold
decreased internalisation of free and EGF-bound receptor
(`fold_ksyn_tumor = 1`, `fold_kint_tumor = 0.1`). Tumour cells number 1% of
normal cells.

```{r figure-5a}
scen <- list(
  "Increased synthesis" = c(fold_ksyn_tumor = 10, fold_kint_tumor = 1),
  "Decreased internalisation" = c(fold_ksyn_tumor = 1, fold_kint_tumor = 0.1)
)
sim_t <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(names(scen), function(nm) {
  dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(c(2, 20), function(d) {
    do.call(solve_dose, c(list(dose_mgkg = d), as.list(scen[[nm]]))) |>
      dplyr::mutate(tumor = nm)
  }))
}))
dplyr::bind_rows(
  sim_t |> dplyr::filter(tumor == "Increased synthesis") |>
    dplyr::transmute(time, dose, cell = "Normal", rl = rl_pct_normal),
  sim_t |> dplyr::transmute(time, dose, cell = paste("Tumour:", tumor), rl = rl_pct_tumor)
) |>
  dplyr::filter(time <= 24 * 80) |>
  ggplot(aes(time / 24, rl, colour = cell, linetype = factor(dose))) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(x = "Time (days)", y = "Active receptors (% of pre-treatment)",
       colour = NULL, linetype = "Dose (mg/kg)",
       caption = "Replicates Figure 5a of Krippendorff 2012.") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.box = "vertical")
```

```{r figure-5b}
spec <- sim_t |>
  dplyr::group_by(tumor, dose) |>
  dplyr::group_modify(function(s, key) {
    mt <- measures(s, "rl_pct_tumor")
    mn <- measures(s, "rl_pct_normal")
    tibble::tibble(S_E = mt[["integral_d"]] / mn[["integral_d"]],
                   S_p = mt[["peak"]] / mn[["peak"]],
                   S_d = mt[["duration_d"]] / mn[["duration_d"]],
                   E_tumor = mt[["integral_d"]], dur_tumor = mt[["duration_d"]])
  }) |>
  dplyr::ungroup()
knitr::kable(spec |> dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(where(is.numeric), ~ signif(.x, 3))),
             caption = "Antibody specificity (Eq. 29), tumour/normal. Compare Figure 5b.")

# A duration of NA means the activated receptors had not recovered to 75% of
# baseline by day 120.
dec <- spec |> dplyr::filter(tumor == "Decreased internalisation")
inc <- spec |> dplyr::filter(tumor == "Increased synthesis")
stopifnot(
  # Paper: decreased internalisation gives stronger inhibition than normal
  # cells, with a higher integral and a longer duration than increased
  # synthesis.
  all(dec$S_E > 1.5),
  all(dec$E_tumor > inc$E_tumor),
  all(dplyr::coalesce(dec$dur_tumor, Inf) > inc$dur_tumor),
  # Eqs. 37-40 are linear in the receptor states for a given Cint(t), so a
  # 10-fold synthesis rate scales every tumour state 10-fold and leaves the
  # relative response identical to normal cells.
  all(abs(inc$S_E - 1) < 1e-4),
  all(abs(inc$S_p - 1) < 1e-4)
)
```

# PKNCA: plasma exposure

The paper reports no NCA, so this block characterises the simulated plasma
profiles (normal cells only, Fig. 3 configuration) for reference; there is no
published comparison.

```{r pknca}
sim_nca <- sim_n |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(id = dose, treatment = paste(dose, "mg/kg")) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, Cc, treatment)
dose_df <- sim_nca |>
  dplyr::distinct(id, treatment) |>
  dplyr::mutate(time = 0, amt = as.numeric(sub(" mg/kg", "", treatment)))
conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(sim_nca, Cc ~ time | treatment + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | treatment + id, route = "intravascular")
intervals <- data.frame(start = 0, end = 24 * 120, cmax = TRUE, auclast = TRUE, half.life = TRUE)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))
nca_tab <- as.data.frame(nca_res) |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "auclast", "half.life")) |>
  dplyr::select(treatment, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES)
nca_tab |>
  dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(-treatment, ~ signif(.x, 3))) |>
  dplyr::rename("Dose" = treatment, "Cmax (ug/mL)" = cmax,
                "AUC0-120d (h*ug/mL)" = auclast, "Terminal t1/2 (h)" = half.life) |>
  knitr::kable()
# Dose-normalised exposure rises with dose (target-mediated disposition).
auc <- setNames(nca_tab$auclast, nca_tab$treatment)
stopifnot(auc[["20 mg/kg"]] / 20 > 1.5 * auc[["2 mg/kg"]] / 2)
```

# Assumptions and deviations

- **`SFiviv` orientation.** Eq. 18 defines `KM,PK = SFiviv KM,cell` and the
  affinity section prints `KD(in vivo) = SFiviv KD(in vitro)`; the two agree
  with each other. The Table 1 and Table 2 values, however, give
  `KM,cell = 7.08 nM` and `KM,PK = 3.38 nM`, so the reported number
  `SFiviv = 2.1` is `KM,cell / KM,PK`, the reciprocal of Eq. 18's factor
  (0.48). The maintainers follow the equations: zalutumumab's in vivo
  `KD = 7 / 2.1 = 3.33 nM`, which makes the cell model's KM equal the
  `KM,PK` of the inherited PK model. The model file stores the printed 2.1
  and divides by it. The evidence: with this choice the 2 mg/kg plasma
  profile agrees with the Michaelis-Menten model within about 10% (the paper
  reports good agreement at all three doses), and the 2 mg/kg nadir of
  activated receptors is 35% of baseline, matching the text's "about 35%".
  Multiplying by 2.1 instead (`KD = 14.7 nM`) puts the 2 mg/kg plasma curves
  more than 300% apart. The cost is a 2 mg/kg peak saturation of 65% against
  Table 3's "Max. 60%".
- **2 mg/kg receptor reduction.** The Results text says the 2 mg/kg dose
  "reduces the number of active receptors by about 35%". The model's nadir
  is 35% of baseline, a 65% reduction that mirrors the 65% peak saturation;
  the sentence is read as "reduces to about 35%". The Fig. 3b image in the
  open-access record is too low-resolution to read the nadir.
- **Tumour specificity for increased synthesis.** The paper states that for
  both tumour alterations the inhibitory effect is stronger in tumour than in
  normal cells. For the increased-synthesis tumour this cannot hold under
  Eqs. 37-40 as printed: the receptor equations are linear in the receptor
  states for a given interstitial concentration, so a 10-fold synthesis rate
  scales every state 10-fold and the relative response equals that of normal
  cells (specificity exactly 1). The decreased-internalisation tumour does
  show the paper's stronger and longer inhibition. No parameter was changed;
  the Fig. 5 image is too low-resolution to compare in detail.
- **`Bmax,PK` units.** Table 1 prints "mg/h/kg"; Eqs. 2-3 use `Bmax,PK` as an
  amount and Eq. 17 reproduces the reported `Ncell = 5.2e9` only with
  2 mg/kg, so the value is used as an amount per kg.
- **Typographical errors in the equations.** Eq. 11 prints `koffC RD` for
  `koffC RC`; Eq. 35 prints `d R_LN/dt` for `d RL_N/dt`. The Fig. 4 caption
  refers to Table 3 for the affinities, which are in Table 4.
- **`CLlin`.** Table 1 gives `CLlin = Vpla kel`, using the rate constant that
  Table 1 describes as "elimination of EGFR by internalisation and
  degradation" (0.0055 1/h). This is encoded as printed.
- **Tumour scenarios.** The model default is the increased-synthesis tumour
  (`fold_ksyn_tumor = 10`). The decreased-internalisation tumour applies the
  10-fold reduction to both `kdegR` and `kdegRL` (Fig. 5 caption, "free and
  bound receptor") after the monkey adjustment of `kdegR`; `kdegRC`,
  recycling and degradation are unchanged. Neither choice is spelled out
  further in the paper.
- **Ligand.** The EGF concentration `L` is held constant (no ODE is given for
  it), as in the paper.
- **Units.** The receptor rate constants are kept in the per-minute units of
  Table 2 and converted to per hour inside `model()`; `kdegRC` and the PK
  parameters are already per hour.
- **Figure 3a observed data** are not reproduced (courtesy data, not
  published); the comparison is against the paper's Michaelis-Menten model.
- **Erratum check.** No correction notice was found in Europe PMC as of
  2026-11-19.
